findings.reason: §5's node should extend `imas_codex/cocos/calculator.py` (survivor-set determination as a generalisation of `determine_cocos`, reusing `cocos_sign` for the class factor) instead of adding a parallel module; the plan as written rebuilds machinery the codebase already has.
findings.text: §5 builds "cocos-determination-core" without citing the existing determiner. `imas_codex/cocos/calculator.py:158 determine_cocos(psi_axis, psi_edge, ip, b0, q, dp_dpsi)` already infers a COCOS value and a confidence from physics observables using the same Sauter Eq. 23 the plan restates in §5, and `:345 validate_cocos_from_data(declared_cocos, ...)` already returns a consistency verdict (`ValidationResult`), `:248 validate_cocos_consistency` returns the per-observable inconsistency list, and `:102 cocos_to_parameters` — which §5 does cite — is in the same module. The plan's survivor-set logic is a generalisation of this single-value determiner, not new physics; proposing `imas_codex/cocos/determination.py` as a sibling hides that the scalar case is a special case of the survivor case and forks the Eq. 23 implementation across two files that must then stay in step. A census of the missed prior art in this family: `imas_codex/cocos/calculator.py:158`, `:248`, `:345`; `imas_codex/ids/transforms.py:43 cocos_sign` (per-class sign between two conventions); `imas_codex/ids/transforms.py:102 compose_transform` (the "map applies one transform, once" mechanism §1 alludes to).

findings.reason: naming the owner lets the author extend it; a forked determiner drifts, and §5's "coefficient classification" would otherwise be written twice.
findings.text: the plan puts COCOS determination in a new file (`cocos/determination.py`, §5 `cocos-determination-core`) rather than extending the module that already owns COCOS identification and validation. `imas_codex/cocos/` is the owner: `calculator.py` holds `cocos_to_parameters`, `determine_cocos`, `validate_cocos_consistency`, `validate_cocos_from_data`, and `__init__.py` re-exports the public surface. A sibling `determination.py` splits the owner across two modules with two confidence conventions and two copies of Eq. 23.

findings.reason: the honest change is an extension of the existing module (add a survivor-set return) rather than a parallel one; the plan should say so or explain the constraint that prevents it.
findings.text: §5's proposed `cocos-determination-core` is a thin layer over existing machinery: a survivor loop that calls the existing scalar determiner per candidate convention. The plan must state why `calculate.py`'s `determine_cocos`/`validate_cocos_from_data` cannot be extended to return the survivor set (they already compute a COCOS and a confidence from the same observables). No such justification appears.

findings.reason: the author should extend `detect_signal_sources`/its keyer (or justify placing a source regroup in the shared layer); as written the correction is placed in a file that does not own the group key, which is how a second grouping key comes to exist.
findings.text: §9 proposes to "regroup" sources by measurement kind in `imas_codex/discovery/base/grouping.py`, but the digit-run keying it means to correct is not owned there. `detect_signal_sources` lives at `imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py:1747` and keys groups through `_accessor_to_source_key(accessor)` (the digit-run rule the plan describes exactly); `imas_codex/discovery/base/grouping.py` is the shared claim/propagate layer whose own module docstring states "Detection algorithms stay in their respective discovery modules". The split/merge-by-kind belongs beside `detect_signal_sources` (make its key kind-aware), or `grouping.py` must be extended as a source-membership owner — the plan names `grouping.py` while describing a defect in `parallel.py`, so the owner it should extend is unstated.

findings.reason: the plan's phrase "claims enriched sources" may already intend `claim_signal_sources`; naming it (as §4 names `judge_rows`) removes the ambiguity, but does not change the design if the intent is reuse.
findings.text: §7's stage "claims enriched sources without a convention status", and §3 adds "claim fields for the stage's claim loop", but neither names the existing claim mechanism: `imas_codex/discovery/base/grouping.py:26 claim_signal_sources` (atomic claim_token two-step claim) and `:92 propagate_source_enrichment` are the shared source claim/propagate primitives. A new claim loop in `imas_codex/cli/discover/conventions.py` would be a second owner of source claiming beside the one that already exists.

findings.reason: without naming the relationship the graph gains two owners of a "cocos" fact at two levels, and the map must later decide which to trust; the section must name what it retires/merges or why both must coexist.
findings.text: §3 adds two new enums (`cocos_class` with nine values, `convention_status` with four), a new node label `ConventionObservation`, and a `cocos`/`cocos_class`/`cocos_survivors`/`cocos_confidence` property family on `SignalSource` — beside `FacilitySignal.cocos` (`imas_codex/schemas/facility.yaml:2595 sign_convention`, `:2599 cocos`), which already exists and is populated on 12 JT-60SA signals per §1. The section does not say whether `FacilitySignal.cocos`/`sign_convention` are retired, migrated to the source, or kept as per-signal overrides.

findings.reason: the section must account for the added interface surface in its own text (or state why no existing stage/command can carry it) before the first implementation node is released.
findings.text: §7 adds `imas-codex discover conventions FACILITY`, a new entry in the stage registry (`imas_codex/cli/discover/sequence.py`), without stating what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be. Against this week's supplied counts (public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0) the section is a pure addition to the CLI-option family.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the §4 judgment (`conventions.py`) and the §5 determination core each hide a substantial decision sequence (four parallel questions per source; sixteen-convention scoring) behind a single module, so the design concentrates behaviour behind interfaces smaller than what they hide.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements two owned mechanisms rather than extending their owners: COCOS determination (owner `imas_codex/cocos/calculator.py`) and source grouping by measurement kind; the latter's keying logic is owned by `imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py:1747 detect_signal_sources`, not by the file §9 names.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §3 (two new enums, a new node type, one new `cocos`/`cocos_class` property family beside the existing `FacilitySignal.cocos`) and §7 (a new `discover conventions` subcommand) each add surface without naming what they retire or merge, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites only `cocos_to_parameters` as prior art, but COCOS identification from physics observables (`imas_codex/cocos/calculator.py:158 determine_cocos`, `:345 validate_cocos_from_data`, `:248 validate_cocos_consistency`) and the per-class sign factor between two conventions (`imas_codex/ids/transforms.py:43 cocos_sign`) already exist and are exactly what §5 proposes to build; the plan searches none of them.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §5's `cocos-determination-core` adds `imas_codex/cocos/determination.py` whose job is a survivor-set variant of the existing scalar `determine_cocos` in `imas_codex/cocos/calculator.py`, and the plan never says why that module cannot be extended instead.
